name: 30 Minute Meals
description:
30 Minute Meals is a Food Network show hosted by Rachael Ray. Her first of four shows on Food Network debuted in the fall of 2001. The show specializes in convenience cooking for those with little time to cook. The show is recorded live-to-tape, with Ray doing almost all preparation in real time. The show was awarded an Emmy for Best Daytime Service Show in 2006.

A common feature on the program is the creation of new versions of classic dishes, some of which are traditionally slow to cook. Ray focuses on creating meals in less than 30 minutes. Ray has also done two specials with the title Thanksgiving in 60, based around the idea of a one-hour Thanksgiving dinner.

Each episode Ray opens the show by saying "Hi there, I'm Rachael Ray and I make 30-minute meals. Now that means in the time it takes you to watch this program, I will have made a delicious and healthy meal from start to finish."

videos.title: Orecchiette with Broccoli Rabe
videos.overview: Rachael Ray pleases all tastes in her family by making orecchiette and broccoli rabe both with and without Italian sausage.

videos.title: Heart, Health, Hearth and Home
videos.overview: Rachael Ray uses the same Dijon and herb breadcrumb mixture on both chicken and halibut, and she makes gnocchi with walnut pesto to serve on the side.

videos.title: Beef Bibimbap with All the Fixings
videos.overview: Rachael Ray makes a Korean-style meal in a bowl, loaded with protein, vegetables, sticky rice and an egg on top.

videos.title: I Can’t Decide Mash-Up: Cheese Soup, Con Carne Chili and Queso
videos.overview: Rachael Ray mashes up Tex-Mex favorites -- queso, chili con carne, tacos and quesadillas -- in one indulgent soup with chorizo, ground beef and a blend of cheeses.

videos.title: BLD for Two: Egg Foo Yung for Breakfast, Lunch or Dinner
videos.overview: Rachael Ray makes her own Chinese-style pork sausage for her oversized vegetable and protein omelets.

videos.title: Everyone's Italian on Sunday: Linguini con Vongole
videos.overview: Rachael Ray includes fresh cherry tomatoes in her linguine with clam sauce.

videos.title: Street Food: Za’atar Chicken or Eggplant and Hummus with Israeli Salad
videos.overview: Rachael Ray makes her favorite Israeli street food, including chicken, eggplant, hummus and an Israeli-style chopped salad.

videos.title: Pasta Alla Boscaiola
videos.overview: Rachael Ray makes a rustic, Tuscan-style mushroom ragu with pasta.

videos.title: Mission: Impossiballs
videos.overview: Rachael Ray uses plant-based meat substitute for her healthier meat-free meatballs. She also makes a marinara sauce and crisp salad to round out the meal.
